## Comparison

Both traces approach the puzzle identically: they identify the same key blocks (Block B: [Maple, 1715, Vellum]–[Elm, 1712, Cloth]; Block A: [1714]–[Palm]; Ash–Leather pair) and systematically test positions for Block B across the six slots. Both eliminate positions 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, and 5-6 for the same reasons, and both converge on Block B at 4-5 with Block A at 1-2. The sibling trace confirms each eliminated branch: when Trace 1 fails B1.1 (Block B at 1-2) due to Rag<1711 and Holly<1713 conflicts, Trace 2 independently fails Case 1 for the same reasons; when Trace 1 finds the solution in B1.4, Trace 2 finds it in Case 4. No divergence in approach or outcome occurs during the solving phase.

The main divergence is in post-solution behavior. Trace 1 verifies once and states the answer twice (a single LOOP). Trace 2 undergoes extensive multi-round re-verification—spot-checking constraints already checked, re-deriving placements already established, and performing a second full 16-clue verification (multiple LOOPs). The sibling trace (Trace 1) demonstrates this re-verification is unnecessary: Trace 1 reaches the same correct answer with a single verification pass, confirming that Trace 2's repeated checks add no new information.

## Trace 1

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's try Sub-case B1.1: Block B is at 1-2." end="So B1.1 is impossible." basis="Block B at positions 1-2 is explored as an alternative and then eliminated due to Rag<1711 and Holly<1713 conflicts; Trace 2 eliminates the same position (Case 1) for the same reasons."⟧

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's try Sub-case B1.2: Block B is at 2-3." end="Therefore, Block B cannot be at 2-3." basis="Block B at positions 2-3 is explored and eliminated because 1716 has no valid position; Trace 2 eliminates the same position (Case 2) for the same reasons."⟧

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's try Sub-case B1.4: Block B is at 4-5." end="So the solution seems unique with the configuration found in B1.4.A." basis="Block B at positions 4-5 is explored and leads to the complete valid solution; Trace 2 confirms this is the only productive branch (Case 4)."⟧

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's quickly check if 5-6 is possible." end="So 5-6 is impossible." basis="Block B at positions 5-6 is explored and eliminated because Maple<1713 cannot be satisfied; Trace 2 eliminates the same position (Case 5) for the same reasons."⟧

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Case B1.4.B: 1714 at 2." end="Thus B1.4.B is impossible." basis="The alternative of placing 1714 at slot 2 is explored and eliminated because 1716 has no valid position; Trace 2 eliminates the same sub-branch (Subcase 4.2)."⟧

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="If Leather at 3: Ash at 3." end="So Leather cannot be at 3." basis="Leather at slot 3 is explored and eliminated because it violates the Leather≠3 constraint, forcing Leather to slot 6."⟧

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Answer: Slot 1: Birch, 1714, Rag" end="Slot 6: Ash, 1713, Leather" basis="The final answer line is stated verbatim twice with no new information added between the two occurrences."⟧
